criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: new tests show an intervention logged with category `mistake` is accepted by the parser and appears in `InterventionCategory::ALL`, and an unknown category is still rejected with an error listing `mistake`.
criteria.evidence: These tests passed: records::tests::mistake_is_a_category_and_in_all (ALL has 9 entries including Mistake), parse_accepts_mistake, and lifecycle.rs intervene_accepts_mistake_and_rejects_unknown_category_listing_mistake. That last test logs a `mistake` through Athena::intervene, then checks that category `blunder` errors with text naming both `blunder` and `mistake`. The plan put that test in manage.rs, but it is in lifecycle.rs. manage.rs did not need a change because the error lists the categories from ALL.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a test with several mistake interventions of different classes and causes shows `athena status` output and its JSON report mistake counts per class and per cause, in fields separate from `interventions_by_category`.
criteria.evidence: Two tests passed. lifecycle.rs status_reports_mistakes_per_class_and_per_cause_apart_from_categories checks StatusView.mistakes, the display::status text, and the `mistakes` key of `athena status --json` (run as the binary), which is separate from interventions_by_category. introspection.rs mistakes_with_the_same_cause_aggregate_into_one_proposal runs the `athena status` binary with 2 distinct causes and checks that the text shows 'mistakes 3: by class: code 2, docs 1' and 'Nothing runs the docs test. 2'. It checks that the JSON has by_class and by_cause, and that interventions_by_category is exactly {"mistake": 3}.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a CLI test in crates/athena-cli/tests (auditor.rs or introspection.rs) runs the audit command and asserts its output reports mistakes per class and per cause. A second case asserts the mistake counts still print when no job audit is produced.
criteria.evidence: These tests passed. auditor.rs the_audit_output_reports_mistakes_per_class_and_per_cause covers the case where an audit is produced, using athena.audit plus display::audit_report. auditor.rs the_audit_output_reports_mistakes_when_no_audit_is_produced is a nested run with audit None and checks the counts and 'no job audit produced'. introspection.rs athena_audit_prints_mistakes_before_any_audit runs the `athena audit` binary in a repository with no job. Its text and --json output show per-class and per-cause counts, including 'no cause recorded'. In main.rs, the mistake report is computed before the audit and printed on the Ok(None) and Err paths.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a test shows that introspecting a `mistake` intervention yields a proposal naming the check or knowledge that would have prevented it, and that mistakes with the same cause aggregate into one proposal.
criteria.evidence: Two tests passed. a_mistake_intervention_is_introspected_with_guidance_for_the_preventing_check_or_knowledge checks that the prompts for mistake and legacy 'Mistake:' records carry mistake_guidance naming check/knowledge and that an ordinary `other` prompt does not. It also checks that the proposal has kind 'check' and the prevention text. mistakes_with_the_same_cause_aggregate_into_one_proposal gives 3 mistakes whose causes differ only by case and punctuation and gets 2 proposals, with the shared one covering 2 mistakes. The status.rs unit test mistakes_count_per_class_and_per_cause_and_same_cause_gives_one_proposal also passed.

criteria.criterion: Existing records with category `other` and text starting 'Mistake:' are counted as mistakes in status and the audit. Records are not rewritten. The text-prefix rule is documented in a code comment or doc.
criteria.evidence: records.rs is_mistake has a doc comment stating the rule: category `mistake`, or `other` with `what` starting "Mistake:" (case sensitive), and no record is rewritten. LEGACY_MISTAKE_PREFIX is a named constant. docs/design/athena-v0.md states the same rule. The lifecycle test a_legacy_other_record_..._not_rewritten passed: it checks the status count, the `athena audit` binary output 'mistakes 1: by class: docs 1', that the record file is byte-identical, and that the category is still `other`.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean, and `cargo test` passes in full.
criteria.evidence: fmt printed nothing. clippy with -D warnings finished with no diagnostics. The full `cargo test --locked` run completed without a tool error. criteria.criterion: Outcome-check: a reader of the status or audit output can see how many mistakes occurred, which classes and causes recur, and which prevention work was proposed. README.md, CHANGELOG.md and the category list in docs/design/athena-v0.md mention the `mistake` category.
criteria.evidence: display::mistakes prints 'mistakes N: by class: …', 'mistakes by cause: …', and one 'prevention (kind, n mistake(s)): <text> · for the cause: <cause> · from introspection <ids>' line per cause. The tests assert these lines in status and audit output. README, CHANGELOG and the category row in athena-v0.md each name `mistake`, and the_readme_changelog_and_design_name_the_mistake_category passed. The fresh-reader rating is prose-only. Reading the output format as a newcomer, it is plain and understandable.

findings.summary: With a job audit produced, no end-to-end test runs the binary; it is covered only through the same library functions main.rs calls.
findings.evidence: auditor.rs the_audit_output_reports_mistakes_per_class_and_per_cause calls athena.audit and display::audit_report directly. The binary `athena audit` is exercised only where no job exists (introspection.rs) and in the legacy lifecycle test.

findings.summary: `athena audit` now fails if loading the mistake report fails, before any audit is tried.
findings.evidence: main.rs Command::Audit runs `let mistakes = athena.mistakes()?;` before athena.audit(&job). A record-load error would stop the audit too. The job audit loads the same records anyway, so the practical risk is low.

findings.summary: Two deliverables listed as 'modify' were not changed: manage.rs and reading.rs.
findings.evidence: git diff HEAD~1 touches 11 files, all on the expected list. The test planned for manage.rs is in lifecycle.rs instead. Every criterion is still shown, and no changed file falls outside the list.

summary: The change does what was asked, and I recommend it pass. It adds a `mistake` intervention category, with legacy `other` records whose text starts 'Mistake:' also counted as mistakes. `athena status`, `athena audit` and their JSON count mistakes per class and per cause, apart from interventions_by_category, and show one prevention line per cause naming whether it is a check or knowledge. Introspecting a mistake asks the model for the check or knowledge that would have prevented it, and mistakes with the same cause share one proposal. The earlier attempt failed on two points, and both are now fixed and tested: tests read the audit output, and the audit prints the mistake report when no job audit is produced (including the binary run in a repository with no job). I ran the 16 new tests and all passed. `cargo fmt --check` and clippy with -D warnings are clean. The full `cargo test` run finished without a tool error; I could not read its saved output under the working-directory policy, but Athena's own run passed 994 tests. All changed files are on the deliverables list. The minor points: with a real job audit, no end-to-end test runs the binary, and the audit now fails if the mistake report cannot load.
